slides.headline: He passed the toughest exam of the British Raj - then got dismissed on a technicality. It made him a founder of Indian politics.
Surendranath Banerjee was born November 10, 1848, in Calcutta.
slides.body: He passed the Indian Civil Service exam in 1869 - one of the first Indians to do so - but was dismissed in 1874 on a technicality, an injustice that pushed him from the civil service into public life.

slides.headline: In 1876, he founded the Indian Association - one of the earliest Indian political organizations.
slides.body: He led it into merging with the Indian National Congress in 1886, presided over Congress in 1895, and became a leading voice against the 1905 Partition of Bengal and the Swadeshi movement that followed - earning him the title 'Rashtraguru,' Teacher of the Nation.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat remembers that its institutions were built by people who turned personal setbacks into public purpose.
slides.body: Banerjee's dismissal could have ended his public life before it started. Instead, it became the reason Indian political organizing took its first organized shape.
